notes.meaning: Love and devotion for Jesus led the women back to the tomb as soon as the Sabbath rest was over. Because Jesus had died late on Friday afternoon, His burial had been done in a hurry, so they brought prepared spices to finish anointing His body properly. God honored their quiet loyalty by making them the very first witnesses of the resurrection.

The women arrived and found the heavy stone already rolled back from the tomb entrance. An angel had moved the stone, but not to let Jesus out, because His risen body was not trapped by physical walls. It was rolled away so people could look in and see that the grave was empty.

The women stepped inside the tomb and were stunned that Jesus was not there. None of the Gospel writers describe the actual moment of the resurrection, only the discovery of the empty tomb. Luke emphasizes that His physical body was missing, showing that Christ truly rose from the dead in bodily form.

While the women were still puzzled over the missing body, two angels appeared before them in dazzling, bright clothes. Their confusion proves they were not expecting a resurrection, showing their testimony was not wishful thinking. Just as angels announced the birth of Jesus to humble people, angels now announce His victory over death to these faithful women.

Overcome with fear and reverence, the women bowed down with their faces to the earth. The angels asked them why they were looking in a graveyard for Someone who is alive. Jesus had conquered the grave, so looking for the living Lord among dead bodies made no sense at all.

The heavenly messengers announced the great truth that Jesus was no longer in the tomb because He had risen. They reminded the women that Jesus had already explained this while they were still with Him in Galilee. Real peace and faith begin when we remember and trust what Christ has spoken.

The angels quoted Jesus's own clear prediction about His arrest, death, and resurrection. Christ's death was not a failure of His mission, but an essential part of God's plan to save sinners from the penalty of their wrongdoing. Jesus had promised from the beginning that He would rise again on the third day.

Hearing the angels' message brought Jesus's own teachings back to the women's minds. Seeing the empty tomb had only confused them, but remembering Jesus's words gave them true understanding. God's truth often bears fruit in our hearts long after we first hear it.

Leaving the tomb, the women hurried to tell what had happened to the eleven apostles and the other disciples. God chose these devoted women to bring the first news of the risen Christ to His fearful followers. Their bold obedience showed how God works through humble servants to proclaim His kingdom.

Luke names several of the women who shared this report, including Mary Magdalene, Joanna, and Mary the mother of James. These were faithful disciples who had supported Jesus during His ministry and stood by Him during His crucifixion. Their united testimony gave clear and credible witness that the Lord was alive.

The apostles thought the women were talking nonsense, like people raving in a fever, and refused to believe them. Grief and shattered hopes had blinded the disciples, leaving them skeptical and afraid. Their deep doubt shows that the early church did not invent the resurrection story out of easy belief.

Peter ran to the tomb to see what had happened for himself. Peering inside, he noticed the linen burial cloths lying neatly on their own without the body, which ruled out a hurried grave robbery. Peter walked away amazed and deeply puzzled, still struggling to understand because he had forgotten Jesus's promise.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars note that a few early manuscripts leave out this verse, though traditional commentators affirm it as a genuine summary of Peter's visit to the tomb.

notes.meaning: Later that same day, two of Jesus's followers were walking to Emmaus, a village about seven miles from Jerusalem. These travelers were not from the eleven apostles, but were ordinary, devoted disciples. Their journey shows that Jesus cares about everyday believers and meets them in their personal grief.

As the two men walked along the road, they talked through all the painful events of the past few days. Their hearts were burdened by Jesus's arrest, trial, and crucifixion, and they tried to make sense of what had happened. Talking honestly with fellow believers about our questions and about Christ is a helpful step toward finding comfort.

While the two disciples were debating the meaning of these events, Jesus Himself came up and began walking alongside them. He joined them as a fellow traveler to comfort them and gently answer their doubts. When Christians gather to talk about the Lord, Christ often draws near with His unseen presence.

God kept the two travelers from recognizing Jesus, even though He was walking right beside them. Jesus veiled His identity so they could speak freely and learn from the Scriptures rather than rely only on physical sight. Our ability to understand spiritual truth depends completely on God opening our eyes.

Jesus asked the travelers what they were discussing with such intensity, which stopped them in their tracks with sorrow on their faces. Even after rising in glory, Jesus is tenderly concerned about the real grief of His disciples. He invites His followers to pour out their sadness so He can minister to their hearts.

Cleopas responded with total surprise, wondering how any visitor in Jerusalem could be unaware of what had just taken place. The trial and crucifixion of Jesus had stirred the whole city during the Passover festival. Cleopas was so absorbed in Christ's death that he assumed everyone else must be talking about it as well.

Jesus gently invited them to explain, and they described Jesus of Nazareth as a great prophet sent by God. They pointed to His powerful miracles and His pure teaching, which had won favor before both God and the people. Even though their hopes were shaken, they still honored Jesus's blameless character and divine authority.

The disciples explained how their chief priests and rulers handed Jesus over to be condemned to death and crucified by the Romans. They were shocked and deeply grieved that their own religious leaders had rejected and killed an innocent man of God. This tragic event seemed to put an end to all their hopes.

Cleopas confessed that they had hoped Jesus was the promised Redeemer who would free Israel from Roman oppression. His death seemed to destroy that hope, leaving them confused and disappointed. They also pointed out that it was now the third day since His death, which was the very day when Jesus had hinted something would occur.

The travelers shared that some women from their company had added to their amazement earlier that morning. These women had visited the tomb at daybreak to care for Jesus's body, only to find the grave already open. Rather than bringing immediate joy, the report had left the disciples thoroughly bewildered.

The women could not find the body and reported that angels told them Jesus was alive. Cleopas and his companion treated this news with doubt, viewing it more like an unbelievable vision than a verified reality. Their hesitation shows how hard it was for them to accept the resurrection without solid proof.

Other disciples, including Peter and John, had gone to the tomb and verified that it was empty, just as the women had reported. But because none of them had actually seen Jesus, the group remained downcast and unsure. Their sadness continued because they were depending on their physical eyes instead of trusting God's promises.

Jesus corrected the disciples for being foolish and slow to believe the writings of the Old Testament prophets. He was not speaking out of cruel anger, but pointing out how their misconceptions had blinded them to God's revealed truth. They were eager to accept the promises of the Messiah's future glory, but had ignored the passages foretelling His suffering.

Jesus explained that the Messiah's painful death on the cross was not an unexpected defeat, but God's required path to save sinners and enter His glory. Prophecies like Isaiah 53 showed that the Christ had to suffer and die to pay for sin before reigning in honor. The very cross that had troubled the disciples was actually the ultimate proof that Jesus was the true Savior.
